audit.name: Independent audit of zero-friction API activity tracking
method: fresh session, fresh worktree, new audit branch
packaged Tethra.app used for the principal onboarding test, copied outside the repository
clean state: no CLI on PATH, isolated HOME and TETHRA_DIR, fresh vault, no prior observations
nine independent reviewers across detection, verification, plan/apply/undo, packaging, UX, validation, gateway security, privacy, IPC/authorization
all CRITICAL and HIGH findings reproduced first-hand by the lead auditor or by an empirical harness
mutation testing against the load-bearing verification assertion

findings.title: Arbitrary code execution when a folder is scanned
findings.affected_user: Every user. In the desktop app the scan runs the instant a folder is picked, so selecting a cloned repository executes attacker code before any confirmation.
findings.reproduction: git init in a folder; git config core.fsmonitor <payload>; add a .env with OPENAI_API_KEY; run `tethra track <folder> --dry-run` from the packaged app. Payload executed 4 times.
findings.expected: detect.rs:12 and AUTOMATIC_PROVIDER_DETECTION.md:141 promise parse-only, nothing executed. The scan banner prints 'nothing executed or uploaded'.
findings.actual: Attacker-controlled code executes with the user's privileges, during --dry-run.
findings.root_cause: detect.rs:347 -> envgov::discover -> git_status_of (envgov.rs:118-139) -> gitrepo::run_git_probe -> Command::new(git). `git ls-files` and `git check-ignore` honour the scanned repository's own core.fsmonitor. safe.directory does not protect: it fires only for repos owned by a different user.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand; crates/tracking/src/detect.rs:347; crates/core/src/envgov.rs:118-139; crates/core/src/gitrepo.rs:123; desktop entry apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:3146
findings.remediation: Stop spawning git during detection. Preferred: replace per-file git probes with an in-process .gitignore parser. Minimum: harden every spawn with -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c protocol.ext.allow=never -c alias.*= and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null. Add a hostile-core.fsmonitor regression fixture.

findings.title: Symlink escape: files outside the selected folder are read
findings.affected_user: Anyone scanning a folder they did not author (clone, template, archive).
findings.reproduction: Symlink proj/package.json to a file outside the folder; run `tethra track proj --dry-run`. Two providers detected at `likely` from outside content.
findings.expected: DETECTION_COVERAGE.md:73,80 - reads only under the selected folder; symlinks never followed out of it.
findings.actual: True for .env files only. package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, root .env* name scans and .github/workflows all escape.
findings.root_cause: Two readers disagree. detect::read_bounded (detect.rs:253-265) applies symlink_metadata refusal AND canonicalize-under-root. stackdetect::read_bounded (stackdetect.rs:63-69) applies neither and uses std::fs::metadata, which follows symlinks.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand; cited lines; test gap at crates/tracking/tests/bounds.rs:117 which covers only a symlinked .env and directory
findings.remediation: Give stackdetect::read_bounded the same symlink_metadata + canonicalize-under-root checks, or inject detect's reader. Add regression tests for symlinked package.json, requirements.txt and pyproject.toml.

findings.title: .env files are read with no size cap
findings.affected_user: Anyone scanning a folder containing a large file named .env* (log spill, DB dump, or a deliberate DoS fixture).
findings.reproduction: 234 MB .env; `/usr/bin/time -l tethra track <dir> --dry-run` -> maximum resident set size 1923170304 (1.92 GB, 8.2x), 1.41 s, and the run reports '0 file(s) read'.
findings.expected: DETECTION_COVERAGE.md:78 - 256 KiB per file; oversized files are counted, never silently dropped.
findings.actual: Read in full before any cap is consulted; a 2 GB .env needs ~16 GB and OOM-kills the process. The honesty counter asserts the file was not read.
findings.root_cause: envgov.rs:182 - std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default() then EnvDocument::parse, with no metadata().len() check. detect::read_bounded checks the cap but only after discover has already read the file.
findings.evidence: Measured first-hand; crates/core/src/envgov.rs:182; crates/tracking/src/detect.rs:266,347. Test bounds.rs:159 asserts skipped_oversized >= 1 with no assertion that the bytes were not read.
findings.remediation: Enforce the byte cap inside envgov::discover before read_to_string; report the file as oversized. Add a test asserting bounded memory.

findings.title: Auto-created route origin taken from repository content; documented confirmation gate not implemented
findings.affected_user: Anyone who runs the tracking flow on a folder they did not fully author.
findings.reproduction: A fixture with NO secrets: package.json naming @supabase/supabase-js and .env.development with SUPABASE_URL=https://attacker-controlled.example.com. Plan says 'create routes: supabase -> https://attacker-controlled.example.com'. Carried through --yes: route MAC'd, enabled, persisted, verification key pushed, .env rewritten.
findings.expected: SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md:76-81 - 'it requires an explicit checkbox (never part of Confirmed auto-config)'.
findings.actual: No checkbox in the CLI; the desktop ships it pre-checked with the origin pre-filled.
findings.root_cause: plan.rs:46-52 auto-fills the confirmation - NeedsOriginConfirm at confidence >= Likely inserts into both sel.include and sel.confirmed_origins. track_cmd.rs:239 consumes it verbatim; the only gate is one bulk confirm at track_cmd.rs:375, satisfied by --yes. Desktop: main.rs:3179, TrackFlow.tsx:96. Likely is reachable from the SDK dependency alone.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand (plan) and end-to-end by a reviewer (apply); cited lines; validate_origin correctly refuses loopback and plaintext http, confirming enforcement is intact and the regression is in provenance
findings.remediation: Drop NeedsOriginConfirm from Selections::defaults; make an inferred origin a hard interactive stop and have --yes refuse it; ship the desktop checkbox unchecked with the destination host as its label; add a regression test that a non-manifest-shaped inferred origin is never auto-included.

findings.title: 'Tracking verified' survives the gateway being dead
findings.affected_user: Every tracked user, whenever the service stops (crash, quit, logout, update, uninstall).
findings.reproduction: pkill the gateway; curl the port -> 000; `tethra track status <proj>` -> 'State: tracking verified - traffic observed'.
findings.expected: A distinct stale or attention state. At this moment the user's application is broken - its .env points at a loopback port with nothing listening.
findings.actual: The product reports success.
findings.root_cause: state::refresh consults only historical event rows (state.rs:357-361). No check of route existence, link existence, env drift, or service liveness, and no bound on observation age. last_observed_at is displayed but never compared to now. diagnose.rs does check these but runs only on the no-traffic branch (track_cmd.rs:492-501, TrackFlow.tsx:170-175). Retention defaults to 7 days, settable to 90.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand; cited lines; a reviewer additionally proved the state survives DELETE FROM gateway_project_links and gateway_routes
findings.remediation: Gate Observed/PartiallyObserved on live route+link existence and a bounded last_observed_at age. Add a distinct stale state.

findings.title: A failed re-run reports 'tracking verified' and erases the failure reason
findings.affected_user: Every user who re-runs the flow on an already-tracked folder and hits any failure. No tampering or privilege required.
findings.reproduction: `tethra track <proj> --yes` fails with 'the service did not answer on 127.0.0.1:55102 within 10 s'; the immediately following `tethra track status` reports 'tracking verified - traffic observed'.
findings.expected: needs_attention, with the recorded reason.
findings.actual: The failed setup is promoted back to verified by the previous run's traffic, and attention_reason is nulled.
findings.root_cause: upsert_setup's ON CONFLICT clause updates only four columns (state.rs:181-185), so applied_at, plan_summary_json and first_traffic_at survive a re-run. NeedsAttention is watchable (state.rs:320-327), so refresh runs against the stale watermark; the derived promotion bypasses the legality table and nulls attention_reason (state.rs:412-421). undo.rs:88-95 has the same defect.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand against the packaged helper; harness output 'H3 assertion failed: a FAILED setup was marked verified by the previous run's traffic'
findings.remediation: Clear applied_at, plan_summary_json and first_traffic_at in the ON CONFLICT branch and on the incomplete-undo branch; never let a derived promotion clear attention_reason; do not promote NeedsAttention without a post-failure observation.

findings.title: track undo after a failed apply silently restores nothing and reports success
findings.affected_user: Anyone whose apply fails after step 6 begins, who then runs the officially recommended recovery.
findings.reproduction: Harness: apply fails at PathCheck after the .env was rewritten; undo reports complete=true, links_restored=0, routes_removed=[]; .env not restored; 2 routes and 2 links left; .env still points at the gateway.
findings.expected: track_cmd.rs:426-429 promises 'Completed steps are left in place; tethra track undo restores everything'; TROUBLESHOOTING.md:69-70 repeats it.
findings.actual: Undo no-ops, reports completion, transitions to not_configured and exits 0.
findings.root_cause: The plan summary is persisted only at step 10 (apply.rs:690-696). Earlier failures leave plan_summary_json NULL, and undo.rs:28-33 uses .unwrap_or_default() rather than treating it as unknown, so both loops iterate empty collections and complete stays true.
findings.remediation: Persist an incremental summary as steps complete, or derive undo's work from ground truth (gateway_project_links rows carry prior_env_json); refuse loudly when the summary is absent but link rows exist.

findings.title: Re-derivation is skipped when the watermark is missing; a row renders verified with zero events
findings.affected_user: The exact adversary the shipped invariant names - any process able to write vault.db.
findings.reproduction: Set state='traffic_observed', applied_at=NULL (both nullable, db.rs:1026). Harness: 'H1 events_in_db=0 watch=Observed state=TrafficObserved'. Same via plan_summary_json=NULL.
findings.expected: state.rs:4-6, verify.rs:10-12, lib.rs:12 and db.rs:1013-1017 all claim a stale or hand-edited row can never overclaim traffic_observed.
findings.actual: One nulled column defeats the entire mechanism.
findings.root_cause: Two early returns before any correction: state.rs:329-331 and state.rs:332-334. check_traffic then reads the uncorrected cached state (verify.rs:140-145).
findings.remediation: Move both early returns after the downgrade decision. A missing watermark is strictly less evidence than zero events and must force awaiting_first_request or needs_attention.

findings.title: Unsupported-project dead end demands terminal commands and manual route creation
findings.affected_user: Every user whose project uses any API outside the three trackable providers.
findings.reproduction: A project using Groq, Mistral, Cohere, DeepSeek, Together, Perplexity with matching SDKs -> 'No trackable APIs detected'; guidance points at `tethra provider list` and `tethra gateway route add`; exit 2.
findings.expected: Acceptance target: 0 terminal commands, 0 manual route creation, 0 internal gateway concepts.
findings.actual: All three violated. For the desktop-only user both commands are unexecutable - the CLI is inside Tethra.app, not on PATH. The desktop equivalent points at 'Advanced -> Gateway internals has the manual route form'.
findings.root_cause: No non-expert fallback exists for an unrecognised provider.
findings.remediation: Provide an in-app 'add this API' path collecting a name and base URL in the tracking flow's own vocabulary, without exposing routes or the gateway; or state the supported-provider scope before the user is led into a dead end.

findings.title: Unknown API credentials are silently dropped from the review screen
findings.affected_user: Every user with more than the three supported providers.
findings.reproduction: 30-API monorepo fixture: the screen headed 'Detected:' lists four providers. The other ~26 credentials appear nowhere - not detected, not unsupported, not unknown, not counted. A filename probe confirmed all 8 .env* variants are scanned, so this is provider coverage, not file skipping.
findings.expected: Unknown APIs surfaced; uncertain detections reviewed without blocking confirmed ones. AUTOMATIC_PROVIDER_DETECTION.md:120-121 promises Unsupported { UnknownProvider }.
findings.actual: UnsupportedReason::UnknownProvider (detect.rs:68) is unreachable from folder content. DETECTION_COVERAGE.md:18 states the opposite of AUTOMATIC_PROVIDER_DETECTION.md.
findings.root_cause: Detection is manifest-gated with no residual reporting path.
findings.remediation: Surface unrecognised secret-shaped variables as an explicit, non-blocking 'not recognised' group with a count. Reconcile the two documents.

findings.title: Coverage is three providers; the product promise does not scale past them
findings.affected_user: Everyone outside OpenAI, Anthropic and Supabase.
findings.reproduction: `tethra provider list` returns five providers; provider-manifests/ holds five .toml files; only openai, anthropic and supabase declare a base-URL environment variable.
findings.expected: A feature titled 'zero-friction API activity tracking' implies coverage of the APIs a developer actually uses.
findings.actual: Three trackable. Several unsupported services (Groq, Together, DeepSeek, Fireworks, Perplexity, Mistral) are OpenAI-compatible and would need little more than a manifest entry.
findings.evidence: Reproduced first-hand; provider-manifests/; openai.toml:49, anthropic.toml:43, supabase.toml:33
findings.remediation: Expand the manifest set to the common OpenAI-compatible providers before shipping this as the primary workflow, or state the three-provider scope prominently in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md, README and the in-app empty state - it is currently in none of them.

findings.title: Existing custom base URL is silently re-pointed to the manifest origin, and raises confidence
findings.affected_user: Anyone behind a corporate LLM gateway, LiteLLM, Azure OpenAI, or a self-hosted proxy.
findings.reproduction: .env with OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://litellm.corp.example/v1 -> 'openai confirmed Automatic', no limitations.
findings.expected: An already-customised base URL should suppress Automatic and surface the existing origin for confirmation; the NeedsOriginConfirm shape already exists.
findings.actual: The user's custom endpoint is what makes the detection Confirmed; the route then forwards to https://api.openai.com. Traffic that was going to the corporate proxy now goes to OpenAI, carrying the user's key. The only warning names the variable and never says the destination changes, and the removed line is masked in the diff.
findings.root_cause: detect.rs:402-431 - the S3 branch reads the value only when gw.origins.is_empty() (Supabase); for OpenAI/Anthropic the variable's mere presence becomes evidence. s1 && s3 then hits the Confirmed arm at detect.rs:583.
findings.remediation: In the S3 branch, when !gw.origins.is_empty() and the value is non-empty, non-loopback and not the manifest origin, emit a limitation and downgrade Automatic to NeedsOriginConfirm with the existing value as the inferred origin.

findings.title: Attribution consent under-discloses the granted capability; the security document's claim is false
findings.affected_user: Every user enabling tracking or resuming attribution through the primary flow.
findings.reproduction: Read the master-password field copy in the Track flow; compare with the Advanced push-key dialog.
findings.expected: SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md section 2 claims the memory-oracle residual is 'carried over verbatim'. ADR 0020 mandates the disclosure. GatewayView.tsx:584-594 does it properly.
findings.actual: TrackFlow.tsx:419-431, DashboardView.tsx:319 and track_cmd.rs:328 describe only the labelling benefit. No oracle, no residency, no drop-on-lock, no scope. The GW-11 standing-relay disclosure was carried over, so the omission is specific to attribution.
findings.root_cause: Consent consolidation moved the password field but not the ADR-0020 disclosure copy.
findings.remediation: Add the oracle-while-resident and dropped-on-lock sentences to the password field help text in TrackFlow, the resume dialog and the CLI step line. Correct SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY.md section 2 and ADR 0022 D10.

findings.title: The tracking flow boots out any existing gateway service (fixed LaunchAgent label)
findings.affected_user: Anyone with more than one Tethra data directory, and anyone running the shipped validation script.
findings.reproduction: Observed live during this audit: a real `tethra track --yes` against an isolated data directory booted out this machine's running gateway (dev.api-tracker.gateway, pid 43853) serving the user's real vault. Restored with launchctl bootstrap; now pid 50655 on the original data directory. No user data lost; the plist was never rewritten.
findings.expected: Installing tracking for one data directory must not disable another.
findings.actual: One login slot per user, with no per-data-directory discrimination.
findings.root_cause: crates/gateway/src/lifecycle/macos.rs:26 - LABEL is the fixed constant 'dev.api-tracker.gateway'. The plist path derives from $HOME but the launchd domain target is the real gui/<uid>. Install does bootout then bootstrap on 'already bootstrapped' (macos.rs:204-221).
findings.remediation: Derive the label from the data directory (hash), or refuse with a clear error when the loaded job's --data-dir differs from the target. This is also the root cause of the validation script's self-weakening foreground mode.

findings.title: Setup screen shows 'Waiting for traffic...' forever after polling has permanently stopped
findings.affected_user: Anyone who takes longer than two minutes to restart their project, or who hits one transient IPC error during the wait.
findings.reproduction: Start tracking, reach 'Configuration applied', wait 120 s, then restart the app and make a request.
findings.expected: The screen flips to 'Tracking verified', or says it stopped watching.
findings.actual: Polling is killed permanently and never resumes; the phase stays 'waiting' and the screen keeps rendering 'Waiting for traffic...' - a claim that is now false. 'Run diagnostics' does not restart the poll. The setup may have actually verified; the dashboard shows the truth while this screen does not.
findings.root_cause: One-shot setInterval lifecycle keyed only on phase.name (TrackFlow.tsx:161-186) with no re-arm path. stopPolling at TrackFlow.tsx:173-176 (cutoff) and :177-180 (any poll error); unconditional render at :495-499.
findings.evidence: Cited lines; no test covers this path
findings.remediation: Resume polling after diagnosis or error, or add a 'Check again' action, and change the muted line to 'No longer watching - run diagnostics or open the dashboard' once polling stops.

findings.title: prior_env_json persists raw URLs including query strings
findings.affected_user: Anyone whose linked base-URL variable previously held a URL with a secret in its query string
findings.reproduction: OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://host/v1?api_key=sk-... then link; SELECT prior_env_json returns the full URL. Canary found at vault.db byte offset 527979.
findings.expected: Forbidden-persistence list covers query-string values and raw URLs containing queries
findings.actual: Path, query and fragment recorded verbatim in plaintext
findings.root_cause: envlink.rs:97-130 - the allowlist inspects only the authority and ignores everything after the first / ? #
findings.remediation: Record scheme+authority only, or set prior_withheld for any value containing ? or # or a non-trivial path; migrate existing rows

findings.title: Masking bypass prints full credentials to stdout and IPC
findings.affected_user: Anyone whose credential value contains a placeholder needle substring
findings.reproduction: DATABASE_URL containing 'db.example.com' with a password in userinfo printed in full by track --dry-run
findings.expected: Never print full credentials in CLI output
findings.actual: Unmasked on context and removed diff lines, and across the Tauri IPC boundary
findings.root_cause: envgov.rs:353-370 skips masking when scanner::is_placeholder_value matches, and that is a substring test (scanner.rs:122-147)
findings.remediation: Only skip masking when the whole value equals or starts with a placeholder pattern, or drop the exemption for context and removed lines

findings.title: Re-apply destroys route provenance
findings.affected_user: Anyone who runs track twice and later undoes
findings.reproduction: apply, re-apply, undo -> routes_removed=[], kept with reason 'existed before this setup (only reused)'
findings.expected: Undo removes routes this setup created
findings.actual: Both routes kept forever with a factually false reason
findings.root_cause: record_applied unconditionally overwrites plan_summary_json (state.rs:285-291); the second apply computes created_routes=[] (apply.rs:443-448)
findings.remediation: Merge summaries on re-apply (union of created_routes), or record creation provenance on the route row

findings.title: Undo never restores a route's prior enabled=false state
findings.affected_user: Anyone who deliberately disabled a route
findings.reproduction: Disable a route, run track (re-enables it), undo -> still enabled
findings.expected: undo.rs:1-2 - restore exactly what track changed
findings.actual: Left permanently re-enabled, reported as 'only reused'
findings.root_cause: apply.rs:438-448 buckets ReEnableRoute as reused; undo.rs:71-76 keeps reused routes
findings.remediation: Record re_enabled_routes separately and re-disable on undo

findings.title: 'Narrowly scoped matching capability' overstates narrowness
findings.affected_user: Anyone relying on the scope claim
findings.reproduction: Read PRODUCT_BEHAVIOR.md:80 against vault.rs:553 and attribution.rs:358-388
findings.expected: Per-project, per-route or per-provider scope
findings.actual: Vault-wide fingerprint key; matcher covers all gateway-linked projects
findings.remediation: Reword to 'matching-only (cannot decrypt), limited to linked projects', or implement per-project matcher scoping

findings.title: Foreground fallback child outlives the app
findings.affected_user: Anyone using the foreground fallback after an install is blocked
findings.reproduction: Trigger install-blocked, choose 'Track while the app is open', quit Tethra -> the gateway serve child is still running
findings.expected: TrackFlow.tsx:589-591 'Tracking then runs only while Tethra is open'; DashboardView.tsx:127 'Tracking pauses when Tethra closes'
findings.actual: Standing relay persists after quit; after a crash an orphan may hold a resident matching key with no lock signal
findings.root_cause: std::process::Child has no kill-on-drop; no impl Drop, no .kill() anywhere; RunEvent::Exit (main.rs:3881-3891) never touches foreground_gateway
findings.remediation: Kill and wait the child in RunEvent::Exit; correct the comment at main.rs:74-76

findings.title: Stale plan leaves .env pointing at a link slug with no DB row
findings.affected_user: Anyone who builds a plan in the desktop and another in the CLI before either applies
findings.reproduction: Build P1 and P2 before any link exists; apply P1 then P2 -> files carry slug B, DB has slug A; every SDK request 404s
findings.expected: Apply refuses or reconciles
findings.actual: Digest passes because output bytes are identical; update_link_env matches 0 rows and silently succeeds
findings.root_cause: envlink.rs:475-513 recompute branch leaves existing_link=true; routes.rs:432-444 does not error on 0 rows
findings.remediation: Set existing_link to reflect whether a row with the approved slug exists; make update_link_env error on 0 rows

findings.title: Digest binds the planned output, not the previewed input
findings.affected_user: Anyone editing a target variable between preview and apply
findings.reproduction: Change OPENAI_BASE_URL between preview and apply keeping quoting shape -> digest passes, edit silently overwritten
findings.expected: envlink.rs:408-410 claims it 'refuses when any file changed since the preview'
findings.actual: Value-only edits to target variables produce byte-identical planned output and pass
findings.root_cause: BLAKE3 over slug + path + new_content only (envlink.rs:386-391)
findings.remediation: Include old_content in the digest, or change the claim to 'applies exactly the previewed bytes'

findings.title: Migration duplicates the project for a manually-configured user
findings.affected_user: A user who created their project without --repo and linked by hand
findings.reproduction: Manual project + manual link, then run track -> second project created, new slug, .env rewritten, old link orphaned
findings.expected: MIGRATION.md - 'Nothing is deleted, duplicated, or re-created'; '.env is not rewritten if it already points at the gateway'
findings.actual: Both claims false on this path; only signal is 'Project: X (will be created)'
findings.root_cause: resolve_project finds the project only via registered repo paths (track_cmd.rs:136-164); the manual gateway link flow never registers the folder; apply.rs:772-779 then creates
findings.remediation: Also check gateway_project_links / tracking_setups referencing .env files under the folder before creating a project, or warn loudly when the .env already carries a Tethra marker for a different project

findings.title: Confirmed is self-confirming after the first link
findings.affected_user: Everyone, on every re-scan
findings.reproduction: OPENAI_BASE_URL set to Tethra's own loopback URL plus the key -> confirmed
findings.expected: Confirmed requires two independent signal classes (DETECTION_COVERAGE.md:43)
findings.actual: Tethra's own artifact satisfies the second class
findings.root_cause: detect.rs:402 registers S3 on the variable name; the loopback guard at :417 suppresses only origin inference
findings.remediation: Skip the S3 push when the value carries the gateway marker (envfile.rs:22) or a loopback host

findings.title: pyproject.toml prefix matching invents SDK dependencies
findings.affected_user: Python projects using a package whose name starts with a provider name
findings.reproduction: dependencies = ["openai-whisper>=20240930"] -> openai likely Automatic, auto-selected
findings.expected: Exact dependency-name match, as requirements.txt already does
findings.actual: starts_with match; openai-whisper is offline speech-to-text and never contacts OpenAI
findings.remediation: Parse the requirement specifier and compare the extracted name for equality

findings.title: Placeholder filter is the only value check
findings.affected_user: Anyone with scratch or example values in .env
findings.reproduction: OPENAI_API_KEY=abcdefgh -> likely + Automatic + auto-selected
findings.expected: Manifest key-format regexes exist (openai.toml:27-40) and should gate S1
findings.actual: Only scanner::is_placeholder_value is consulted - length >= 8, twelve English needles, template brackets
findings.remediation: When the manifest has detection patterns, require one to match for S1

findings.title: Detection cost unbounded in file count
findings.affected_user: Monorepos, vendored trees, large folders
findings.reproduction: 300 .env files in a git repo -> 16.5 s; 2000 .env files -> 39.9 s
findings.expected: A file, byte or time budget
findings.actual: Depth is capped at 6; file count, total bytes and wall time are not. Up to 4 git spawns per discovered file, each with a 30 s timeout
findings.root_cause: envgov.rs:144-199; gitrepo.rs:73; SKIP_DIRS covers only 6 names
findings.remediation: Cap discovered-file count and cumulative bytes; batch the git status query; add a wall-clock budget with an honest 'scan truncated' flag

findings.title: Activity summary is global; per-project attribution is unanswerable
findings.affected_user: Anyone tracking two or more projects
findings.reproduction: Track two folders, generate traffic from both, open Activity
findings.expected: Requests, tokens and cost attributable per project
findings.actual: GatewayActivitySummary has no project or provider dimension; the headline grid blends all projects
findings.remediation: Add per-project and per-provider grouping to the summary command and render a breakdown row per tracked project

findings.title: Raw internal enum tokens rendered on the primary dashboard
findings.affected_user: Anyone who enables attribution
findings.reproduction: Enable attribution, generate traffic, open Activity -> 'matched_fingerprint - 12', 'unavailable - 4'
findings.expected: Human-readable labels
findings.actual: DB labels rendered verbatim with no explanation
findings.evidence: Cited lines; no test covers this section
findings.remediation: Map each state to a human string

findings.title: Swallowed error hides a coverage warning
findings.affected_user: Anyone using the foreground fallback
findings.reproduction: Make trackingForegroundActive throw while foreground mode is active
findings.expected: A distinct 'could not determine tracking mode' state
findings.actual: catch { setForeground(false) } - the banner disappears and the user believes background tracking covers them after closing the app
findings.remediation: Render a distinct failure line; also wrap App.tsx:169-173 lockNow, which has no catch at all

findings.title: .env marker comment tells the user to run a command they do not have
findings.affected_user: Desktop-only users
findings.reproduction: Any apply; the comment says 'or run: tethra gateway status'
findings.expected: No terminal commands, no internal gateway concepts
findings.actual: Unexecutable instruction naming internal concepts, written into the user's committed source tree
findings.remediation: Point at the in-app Activity screen instead

findings.title: Marker comment emitted twice per file; stray bare path line in the diff header
findings.affected_user: Everyone
findings.reproduction: Any dry-run
findings.expected: One comment per file; two header lines
